deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from p.5): X is a topos, X_0 ⊂ X an open subtopos (a subobject of the final object), and X_1 the complementary closed subtopos. Equivalently, X comes with a morphism π: X → Top(Δ_1), the Sierpinski topos, with X_0 = π^{-1}(open point {0}) and X_1 = π^{-1}(closed point {1}).

This page states the standard Artin-gluing (recollement) dictionary: the pair (X, X_0) is the same as a triple (X_0, X_1, φ). Here φ: F(X_0) → F(X_1) is a left exact ('exact à g.') and 'accessible' functor; in the open/closed notation φ = i^* j_*. X is recovered as the comma category of triples (F_0, F_1, u: F_1 → φ(F_0)). The marginal '[f_* / f^*]' signals that the model case is φ = f_* for a morphism f: X_0 → X_1. In that case X is the topos-theoretic mapping cylinder, with a retraction X → X_1. This matches the previous page, where the locally constant sheaves on X are the triples (F_1, f^*F_1, tautological u).

The problem: find conditions on (X_0, X_1, φ) under which both inclusions X_0 → X ← X_1 are weak (homotopy) equivalences of topoi. The zigzag X_0 → X ← X_1 is then a 'homotopy correspondence' between X_0 and X_1.

The main case: φ commutes with arbitrary (projective) limits, i.e. φ = f_* has a left adjoint f^*.
- In the earlier §§, f^* was also assumed left exact, so f was a genuine geometric morphism.
- Grothendieck explicitly drops that assumption here, so f^* is merely colimit-preserving.

Special case: X = Top(X) for a small category X. Then X_0 = Top(X_0) and X_1 = Top(X_1) (X_0 a sieve, X_1 the complementary cosieve). As the next page says, f^* is determined by a functor X_1 → X_0^ (presheaves on X_0), extended by colimits, i.e. by a profunctor h: X_0^op × X_1 → Ens. X is then the collage (cograph) of h: a category over Δ_1 with fibres X_0 and X_1 and Hom(x_0, x_1) = h(x_1, x_0). One checks that presheaves on this collage are exactly the triples (F_0, F_1, F_1 → φF_0), where φ(F_0)(x_1) = Hom(h(x_1, ·), F_0). This φ preserves all limits.

So the page sets up the question: when is a profunctor / correspondence between small categories (a category over Δ_1) such that both fibre inclusions are weak equivalences? The aim is to use such correspondences as weak equivalences in the homotopy theory of (Cat) and of topoi.
errors: As transcribed, 'φ = f^* ... i.e. a un adjoint à droite f_*' is mathematically inconsistent with the rest of the passage. A functor commuting with arbitrary projective limits has a LEFT adjoint. And gluing along a φ that need not be left exact would not give a topos. The coherent reading is 'φ = f_*, i.e. φ has a left adjoint f^*', with the parenthetical saying f^* was assumed left exact in the earlier §§. Either the transcription or Grothendieck's hasty annotation swapped f^*/f_*.

'Exact à g.' for φ alone does not suffice for the glued category to be a Grothendieck topos; one needs accessibility. Grothendieck flags this with the word 'accessible', so this is not an error, only a terse condition.
No criterion for the weak equivalences is given on this page; the question is only posed.

ideas.what: Open subtopos ⇔ morphism to the Sierpinski topos Top(Δ_1); (X, X_0) ⇔ glueing data (X_0, X_1, φ) with φ left exact and accessible
ideas.modern_name: Artin gluing / recollement of topoi; Sierpinski topos classifies open subtopoi
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin, Grothendieck, Verdier (SGA4 IV §9.5); Wraith (1974); Johnstone (Topos Theory 1977, Elephant A4.5, A2.1.12 on accessibility)

ideas.what: Gluing along f_* for a morphism f: X_0 → X_1, giving a topos-theoretic mapping cylinder with retraction onto X_1
ideas.modern_name: Mapping cylinder of a geometric morphism (Artin glueing along f_*)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in topos theory (Johnstone; Moerdijk's work on homotopy of topoi)

ideas.what: Dropping left exactness of f^*: gluing along any limit-preserving φ; for presheaf topoi this corresponds to a profunctor h: X_0^op × X_1 → Ens and the category X over Δ_1
ideas.modern_name: Collage/cograph of a profunctor; 'correspondences' = categories over Δ^1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bénabou (distributeurs), Street (collages); Lurie HTT §2.3.1 for ∞-categorical correspondences

ideas.what: Problem: conditions making both inclusions X_0 → X ← X_1 weak equivalences, i.e. correspondences that are homotopy equivalences
ideas.modern_name: Weak-equivalence correspondences / homotopically invertible profunctors; Quillen Theorem A–type asphericity conditions (e.g. contractible categories of elements of h(x_1, ·))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (Theorem A); Thomason; Cisinski (asphericity, Les préfaisceaux comme modèles des types d'homotopie, 2006)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related material in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs (asphericity), but not this formulation to my knowledge

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a programme to treat open/closed decompositions of topoi, equivalently correspondences over the Sierpinski topos, as homotopy equivalences. He explicitly allows the gluing functor to come from a non-left-exact f^*, i.e. an arbitrary profunctor between small categories. This places profunctors/correspondences inside the homotopy theory of (Cat) and of topoi via Top(Δ_1). The page poses the criterion question but does not answer it.
missed.quote: On s'intéresse à des conditions sur (X_0, X_1, φ) qui assurent que les deux inclusions X_0 → X ← X_1 sont des équivalences faibles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a topos-level precursor of the 'correspondence' viewpoint (categories over Δ^1) central to Lurie's HTT and of the asphericity criteria in Cisinski's work. The topos-theoretic formulation over Top(Δ_1), covering non-presheaf topoi, is less explored, but the content largely parallels known theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The gluing dictionary is standard (SGA4). The collage interpretation of profunctors is known (Bénabou/Street). The homotopical question of when correspondences are weak equivalences was later developed by Quillen/Thomason/Cisinski/Lurie. It is mildly interesting to see Grothendieck in the early 1980s deliberately relaxing to non-exact f^* to capture profunctors in the homotopy theory of topoi, but nothing here is finished or clearly absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Marginal '[f^* ||]' over φ is more plausibly '[f_* ||]' (φ = f_*), consistent with the previous page's triples (F_1, f^*F_1, u) and the next page's f^*: X_1^ → X_0^.

'cas où φ = f^* commute en fait aux limites quelconques ... i.e. a un adjoint à droite f_*' should likely read 'φ = f_* ... i.e. a un adjoint à gauche f^*'. Only this makes the following remark about f^* being left exact in the previous §§ coherent.
'foncteur exact à g.[?]' = 'foncteur exact à gauche'; 'accessible' is the next annotation, not part of a garbled word.
